title: Nikon microscopic video competition winner disqualified for using generative AI
slides: Nikon's winner got disqualified — was it fake?
Contest banned generative AI in 2024 rules
But the image was actually a real microscope photo
Judges couldn't tell AI from real science
If experts can't tell, how can you?
thread_text:
1. The Image That Fooled Experts

A Nikon photo contest winner was disqualified for looking AI-generated. But the photo was real — a microscope image of a mouse brain.

2. The 2024 Rule Change

The contest banned generative AI entries only this year, after AI images began flooding competitions. The judges were on high alert for anything suspicious.

3. What the Photo Actually Was

It was a real fluorescence microscope image of neurons. The judges mistook its intricate, surreal patterns for AI. The photographer lost the prize unfairly.

4. Experts Can't Tell Either

If trained judges can't distinguish AI from real science, how can anyone? This isn't about technology — it's about human perception limits.

5. Test Yourself Today

Open an AI image generator and try to create a fake microscope photo. Then ask a friend if it's real. If they can't tell, we have a problem.
